name: Cyclone-4M
description: Three-stage small launch vehicle for Spaceport Nova Scotia (Canso). Values are taken from the Cyclone-4M SLS Abbreviated User's Guide where it states them, and are flagged ASSUMPTION with the reasoning recorded where it does not.

guide.title: Cyclone-4M SLS Abbreviated User's Guide, Version 2

t_to_inj_source: BOUNDED. Cyclone-4M Abbreviated User's Guide v2 (2019-05-15), section 2.4.2 Table 2.1 (200 km orbit at 51.6 deg): Stage 2 ME ignition T+261 s, ME cutoff T+708 s, LJS thruster cutoff T+767 s, then 'TBD, mission specific: SC separation. Stage 2 passivation'. First stable orbit exists at LJS cutoff, so the earliest plausible injection is T+767 s and it is adopted. Latest plausible injection adds the section 2.9 separation allowances: SC separation 15 s after delivery plus the Stage 2 attitude manoeuvre of up to 4 min (240 s) plus the 10 s command delay, then the SSO profile coast and second burn of section 2.5.1 Table 2.2 (ME second cutoff T+4021 s, LJS 42 s to T+4063 s, plus 15 s plus 28 s settling, T+4106 s). Shift sensitivity d(shift)/dT = nodal_rate/24/sweep_rate: +0.164 s per min at SSO drift (+0.9856 deg/day), -0.842 s per min at -5.1354 deg/day (600 km). Accessed 2026-10-04 via Wayback capture 20200615045624.

ascent_profile.source: Cyclone-4M Abbreviated User's Guide v2 (2019-05-15): LEO events from section 2.4.2 Table 2.1 (PLF jettison T+252 s, stage 1 separation T+259 s, Stage 2 ME ignition T+261 s, ME cutoff T+708 s, LJS cutoff T+767 s); SSO events from section 2.5.2 Table 2.2 (PLF jettison T+243 s, stage 1 separation T+261 s, ME first ignition T+262 s, first cutoff T+696 s, ME second ignition T+4008 s, second cutoff T+4021 s). SC separations add section 2.9 (15 s after delivery; manoeuvre up to 4 min; command no less than 10 s after manoeuvre end). Accessed 2026-10-04 via Wayback capture 20200615045624.

downrange_bounds_km.meaning: distance from pad to the stage 1 and fairing impact point, not a half-axis

hazard_footprint.source: Downrange: Registration Document June 2018 section 2.2.5.4 (p.23): the C4M 'drops the first stage and the upper stage fairing just over 2,000 km south of the launch site'. Cross-range: no published figure in the Registration Document, the Focus Report March 2019, the EA approval Conditions June 4 2019, or MLS range-safety material checked 2026-10-04; bounded from corridor geometry. Recorded derivation in cross_range_bound_rationale. Pad radius: Focus Report March 2019 section 12.0 (p.12-3): 'a radius of less than 500 metres surrounding the launch pad' per US DoD Explosives Safety Manual 6055.
hazard_footprint.downrange_rationale: Registration Document June 2018 section 2.2.5.4 (p.23): the vehicle 'drops the first stage and the upper stage fairing just over 2,000 km south of the launch site'. This is the distance to the impact point, not an ellipse half-axis; recorded as such so the model class cannot misread it.
hazard_footprint.cross_range_bound_rationale: Lower bound 100 km: half of the adopted downrange scaled by the corridor fan half-width (55 deg span at 200 deg vs 90 deg gives sin(55 deg)=0.82 lateral fraction; the along-track dispersion of a 260 s stage at 2 km/s is order 50 to 100 km, so 100 km is the floor). Upper bound 340 km: the drop-zone map Figure 2.1 ground tracks for 51.6/87.9/98.1 deg span about 20 deg of longitude at the impact latitude (2000 km downrange); 20 deg at 40 N is about 1700 km wide, and one fifth of that (single-azimuth dispersion) is 340 km. Adopted 200 km is the midpoint rounded, inside both bounds. No invented precision: the bound not the point value carries the information.

published_azimuths.context: SC insertion into a 200 km orbit inclined at 51.6 deg
published_azimuths.source: Cyclone-4M Abbreviated User's Guide v2 section 2.4.1 (p.10): 'The launch azimuth Al = 118.5 deg'. Re-verified against the fetched guide 2026-10-04.

published_azimuths.context: SSO insertion, with a cross-range manoeuvre to the right at T+75 s to bypass Little Dover
published_azimuths.source: Cyclone-4M Abbreviated User's Guide v2 section 2.5.1 (p.12): 'the ILV launch azimuth is 180 deg'. Re-verified against the fetched guide 2026-10-04.

published_azimuths.context: approximate trajectory used for the sonic boom overpressure study, 6.9 psf at 60 km
published_azimuths.source: Nova Scotia Registration Document June 2018, Project 16-5903, section 5 (noise study: 'based on an approximate launch trajectory of 181 deg'). Re-verified in the fetched registration text 2026-10-04.

lateral_manoeuvre.source: Cyclone-4M Abbreviated User's Guide section 2.3: 'For launches into orbits with inclination less than 45.1 deg, the Cyclone-4M can perform a lateral manoeuvre at the equator.' This is the vehicle guide's own note on the impossibility the engine reports, and it is cited in the response provenance.

advertised_inclinations_source: Cyclone-4M Abbreviated User's Guide v2 section 2.3 (p.9): orbits 'inclined at 45.1 deg up to inclinations of sun-synchronous orbits', with Figure 2.1 ground tracks 'for SC injection into orbits inclined at 51.6, 87.9, and 98.1 deg'. Re-verified against the fetched guide 2026-10-04.
paired_profile_rationale: A second profile with a published-coast ascent, so the fixed-point tests can prove that T_to_inj flows through the solver rather than being a constant in it.

rows.source: Guide v2 Table 2.1 LJS cutoff T+767 s (earliest, adopted) to Table 2.2 second LJS cutoff plus section 2.9 allowances T+4106 s (latest); see t_to_inj_source.
Cyclone-4M Abbreviated User's Guide v2 section 2.5.2 Table 2.2 (p.13) and section 2.4.2 Table 2.1 (p.11): liftoff T+9 s
Cyclone-4M Abbreviated User's Guide v2 section 2.5.2 Table 2.2 (p.13) and section 2.4.2 Table 2.1 (p.11): stage 1 separation T+261 s (LEO table T+259 s separation event, T+261 s ME ignition)
Focus Report March 2019 section 12.0 (p.12-3): radius of less than 500 m per DoD 6055
Registration Document June 2018 section 2.2.5.4 (p.23): first stage and fairing drop just over 2,000 km south; recorded as distance to impact point.

No published figure in Registration Document, Focus Report, EA Conditions, or MLS range-safety material (checked 2026-10-04). Bounded 100 to 340 km from corridor geometry; adopted 200 km. See cross_range_bound_rationale.
